title: PRD: Controlled Egress, Upgrade Orchestration, and Air-Gap Compatibility for Private/VPC
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: This PRD defines requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customers who require strict outbound network controls (egress), coordinated offline upgrade flows, and formal air-gap compatibility. The goal is to provide a prescriptive operational model that lets platform and security teams deploy Redwood Private in environments with minimal or no internet egress while still supporting safe upgrades, signed artifacts, and demonstrable rollback procedures. The document focuses on networking allowlists, artifact delivery options (registry mirror, air-gapped bundles), in-place upgrade orchestration, and verification checks. Non-goals include changes to the hosted control plane or adding new runtime features unrelated to networking or upgrades.
non_goals: Does not introduce a new licensing model. Does not change hosted API behaviour. Does not add new hardware provisioning automation (handled by infra teams).
requirements: R1: Provide a minimal egress allowlist template (CIDR/hostnames/ports) that customers can paste into VPC egress policies. Template must be environment-agnostic and include fallback variants for isolated air-gapped installs.

R2: Support three artifact delivery modes for upgrades: (a) direct egress to Redwood artifact registry, (b) customer-hosted registry mirror (OCI/APT/YUM), (c) signed offline upgrade bundle that can be transfered via removable media or secure file transfer.

R3: Upgrade orchestration must support a canary + phased rollout with automatic health checks and automated rollback on failure. Orchestration must not require internet access in the offline bundle mode.
R4: All bundles and images must be cryptographically signed and verifiable offline; the platform must validate signatures prior to applying an upgrade.
R5: Provide a small reference implementation and runbook for customers to host an internal registry mirror and to seed an air-gapped bundle (docs + scripts).

R6: Telemetry collection must be opt-in for private installs; default for air-gapped installs is telemetry off. When enabled, telemetry must not leak sensitive payloads and must be documented in the runbook.

R7: Define automated network tests that validate the allowlist prior to install (DNS resolution, TLS certificate checks, and TCP handshake tests) and a post-upgrade verification suite (runtime readiness, KV cache integrity, latency smoke test).
R8: Upgrade retention policy: the platform must retain upgrade artifacts locally for a configurable retention window to enable quick rollback without external download.
R9: Provide RBAC guardrails in the upgrade process: only users with 'upgrade' permission can initiate bundles; audit logs must record signatures and user IDs.

R10: Documentation and acceptance criteria must include explicit instructions for network operators on ports/protocols required during preflight, install, and upgrade phases, with examples for major cloud providers and on-prem firewalls.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Egress allowlist template published in docs repo and validated by engineering tests. Template includes hostnames, IP ranges, ports, and DNS/CIDR fallback recommendations.
AC-2: Customer can upgrade a Private deployment in three modes: direct, mirror, and offline bundle. Conformance tests must pass for each mode in CI (mocked networks).

AC-3: Offline bundle flow: create-bundle -> transfer to target environment -> validate-signature -> run-upgrade results in a successful upgrade with no internet access. CI run replicates this using containerized network isolation.

AC-4: Phased upgrade orchestration: canary (10% nodes) -> health checks pass -> remainder rollout. If any canary health check fails, system automatically rolls back to previous version within 15 minutes and surfaces incident log in console.
AC-5: Signing and verification: all images and bundles fail validation when signature is tampered; validation errors block upgrades and are surfaced with clear remediation steps.

AC-6: Network preflight tests run and report clear pass/fail statuses. At least three tests (DNS resolve, TLS handshake to allowed host, TCP connect to allowed port) must pass before install proceeds. Failure modes documented.

AC-7: Telemetry default off for air-gapped installs; enabling telemetry requires explicit flag in config and documented privacy checklist. When enabled, example telemetry payloads are reviewed and approved by security.
AC-8: Audit log entries for upgrade initiation contain: user id, bundle signature hash, timestamp, and node targets. Logs must be queryable via Console within 5 minutes of action.

AC-9: Post-upgrade verification suite completes within defined SLA for a small cluster (60s for readiness checks, KV integrity within 5 minutes). Failure triggers automatic rollback and an actionable error message.
AC-10: Runbook and scripts for registry mirror and bundle generation published; at least one customer onboarding test uses the runbook successfully (internal validation).
networking_tests: Preflight-DNS: resolve registry.redwood.ai and mirror.example.local; record TTLs and errors.
Preflight-TLS: establish TLS handshake to allowed hosts using system CA bundle; validate certificate chains.
Preflight-TCP: open TCP connections to required ports (443 for artifact pulls, 22 optional for debug) and measure handshake latency.
Isolation-test: run upgrade using an isolated network namespace (no default route) to validate offline bundle behaviour.
Post-upgrade-smoke: verify REST endpoints respond, KV cache warmup completed, and simple generation API returns expected token lengths.
Audit-log-check: ensure upgrade events are written to audit store and visible in Console within 5 minutes.
upgrade_flow_glossary: bundle: a signed tarball containing images, manifests, and a manifest.json with checksums and signatures.
mirror: a customer-hosted OCI registry or OS package mirror seeded with Redwood artifacts.
canary: initial subset of nodes targeted during phased rollout for safety checks.
health-checks: automated probes (pod readiness, CPU/mem anomalies, API responses) that determine success/failure of a rollout.
rollback: automated revert to a previous version triggered by failed health checks or explicit operator action.
